dublinCore.description: Interactive MicroSim for placing the poles and zeros of a continuous-time transfer function in the s-plane. It shows the magnitude and phase of H(jw) along the jw axis from the vectors to a moving marker, the unit-step response from a numerical simulation of the real-coefficient system, a left-half-plane stability banner, the shaded ROC of the causal system, and an optional inset that maps the poles and zeros to the z-plane with z = e^(sT).

searchKeywords: frequency response from pole zero vectors

learningObjectives: Calculate the poles -zeta wn +/- j wn sqrt(1 - zeta^2) of a second-order system and predict its step overshoot exp(-pi zeta / sqrt(1 - zeta^2))
Determine whether a causal system is stable from its pole locations, and relate this to whether the ROC Re(s) > max Re(p_k) contains the jw axis
Explain |H(jw)| and the phase of H(jw) in terms of the lengths and angles of the vectors from the zeros and poles to the point jw
Distinguish a right-half-plane zero from a right-half-plane pole by its effect on stability, phase and step response
Apply z = e^(sT) to map s-plane poles to the z-plane and identify when a pole aliases (|w| T > pi)
prerequisites: Complex numbers in rectangular and polar form
Step responses of first-order and second-order systems

misconceptions.misconception: A right-half-plane zero makes the system unstable
misconceptions.correction: Stability depends only on the poles; a right-half-plane zero adds phase lag and makes the step response start in the wrong direction
misconceptions.evidence: The Right-half-plane zero preset is reported STABLE, but its step response dips to -0.33 at t = 0.41 s; moving the zero from +1 to -1 keeps |H(j1.5)| = 0.800 but changes the phase from -149.5 to -36.9 degrees

misconceptions.misconception: If the output does not blow up, the system is stable
misconceptions.correction: Simple poles on the jw axis give a bounded impulse response but the system is not BIBO stable
misconceptions.evidence: The Integrator preset turns a unit step into a ramp (y(10 s) = 10), and the Oscillator preset never stops oscillating; both are reported as marginally stable

accessibility.screenReaderScript: An s-plane with sigma on the horizontal axis and j omega on the vertical axis. Poles are red crosses and zeros are blue circles that can be dragged; the region of convergence of the causal system is shaded to the right of the rightmost pole and a banner reports stability. Three plots show the magnitude and phase of H(j omega) for omega from 0 to 4 rad/s and the unit-step response. A gold marker on the j omega axis, set by a slider or by hovering over the frequency plots, shows the vectors from every pole and zero. An optional inset maps the poles and zeros to the z-plane with z = e^(sT).

controls.label: System
controls.description: Loads a preset set of poles and zeros

controls.label: Add pole
controls.description: Adds a pole pair (or one real pole when 'as conjugate pair' is unchecked), up to six poles

controls.label: Add zero
controls.description: Adds a zero pair (or one real zero); disabled when zeros would outnumber poles

controls.label: Remove
controls.description: Deletes the selected pole or zero item

controls.label: as conjugate pair
controls.description: When checked, Add pole and Add zero create a complex-conjugate pair; otherwise a single real root

controls.label: Damping zeta
controls.description: Sets the damping ratio of the selected pole pair, keeping its natural frequency

controls.label: Natural freq. wn
controls.description: Sets the natural frequency (distance from the origin) of the selected pole pair, keeping its damping ratio

controls.label: Marker s = jw
controls.description: Moves the marker along the jw axis; the frequency plots and read-outs give H at this frequency

controls.label: Map to z-plane
controls.description: Shows an inset with every pole and zero mapped by z = e^(sT) and shades the s-plane outside the strip |w| < pi/T

controls.label: T
controls.description: Sampling period T used by the z-plane map

visualElements.description: s-plane with draggable poles and zeros, the jw-axis marker with vectors from every root, and the shaded ROC of the causal system
Magnitude |H(jw)| in dB and phase of H(jw) for w from 0 to 4 rad/s with a marker cursor
Unit-step response with final value, peak marker, overshoot, settling time and second-order formula read-outs
Stability banner, transfer function H(s) with numeric coefficients, selected root read-out and z = e^(sT) inset

model.description: Builds H(s) = K B(s)/A(s) from the poles and zeros (conjugate pairs as real quadratic factors), with K = A(0)/B(0) so that H(0) = 1. H(jw) is evaluated from the vectors jw - z_k and jw - p_k; the unit-step response is integrated with fourth-order Runge-Kutta in controllable canonical form. A causal system is stable when every pole has a negative real part; the ROC is Re(s) > max Re(p_k).
equations: H(s) = K prod(s - z_k) / prod(s - p_k)
p = -zeta wn +/- j wn sqrt(1 - zeta^2)
z = e^(sT), |z| = e^(sigma T), angle z = w T
algorithms: Fourth-order Runge-Kutta integration of the state-space model

instructionalStrategies: Predict pole locations and overshoot before moving the sliders
Read |H(jw)| from vector lengths and check it against the read-out
Contrast stable, marginal and unstable systems through the ROC
extensions: Compare the matched z-transform with the bilinear transform for the same analog prototype
Add a feedback gain and trace the closed-loop poles (root locus)
